note: Self-test of the bench on the synthetic fixture tree built by make_fixture_tree.py, not of any real suite. Each row pins one way the bench must read a mutation: a property red, a form red, a red that lands only on sibling tests, a skip gained under the mutation, and bytes that change while nothing goes red. The absent-anchor row lives in spec_fixture_st1.json, because item 0 refuses an absent anchor and that row exists to be run with --skip-preflight.

mutants.property: BENCH: a mutation that reaches the property reads KILLED through the assertion of the named test; the rewrite keeps the length and the fixture ships a bytecode cache of the original, so the caches must be removed for the suite to see it
BENCH: a mutation that breaks a name reads BROKEN, never KILLED
BENCH: reds that land only on tests the row does not name read KILLED_ELSEWHERE, not KILLED
BENCH: a test skipped under the mutation that ran at baseline makes the run BROKEN, not a survivor
BENCH: bytes that change while every test stays green read SURVIVED
